research_method.claude: Repository mining of commit logs (git log) with SentiStrength-SE sentiment analysis, descriptive analysis and Pearson correlation; 5 RQs
research_method.nlm: Repository mining: quantitative analysis of commit logs with SentiStrength-SE and Pearson correlation; 5 RQs
research_method.value: Repository mining of commit logs (git log) with lexicon-based sentiment analysis (SentiStrength-SE) of 86,515 commit messages; descriptive analysis by team size, change-activity type, commit contribution and time, plus Pearson correlations; 5 RQs

context.value: OSS; seven popular GitHub projects with more than 10 years of history (PostgreSQL, Glibc, Eclipse-CDT, GNUCash, WordPress, Firebug, Rhino); 86,515 commit messages

cat_productivity.note: Sentiment-productivity link argued from literature only; no productivity metric.

cat_quality.note: NotebookLM labels project size (LOC) 'Quality/Product', but it is a size descriptor, not a quality metric.

cat_collaboration.note: Borderline: both label team size / active developers per year as Collaboration, but these are contributor counts derived from commits.

cat_satisfaction.note: Developer sentiment (positive/negative/neutral) in commit messages and sentiment volume.

cat_activity.note: Commit contribution, commits per year, change-activity types (add/delete/modify).

cat_delivery.note: NotebookLM labels commit contribution 'Activity/Delivery', but it is a commit share, not a delivery metric.

cat_agile.note: NotebookLM labels change-activity type 'Process/Activity', but it is a file-change classification, not a process metric.

cat_survey.note: Sentiment is detected automatically from commit text; no perceptual instrument.

evidence.quote: We examined a total of 86,515 commit messages of seven OSS projects to analyze developers' sentiments in commit logs.
evidence.loc: PDF p. 8 (4. Results and analysis, RQ1)

evidence.quote: The commit logs of the projects were retrieved using the git log command.
We applied Pearson Correlation to identify the correlation between commit contribution and sentiments (positive, negative, and neutral).

The projects were selected based on popularity, size, number of commits, number of contributors involved, long project history (more than 10 years), and having a valid Git (distributed version control system) repository.
Our study uses the Sentistrength-SE [15] tool to detect polarity of sentiments conveyed in commit logs messages.
Commit contribution is the percentage of commits made by each individual contributor in a project.
